volatility.definition: How much and how fast a price swings up and down. High volatility means big jumps in both directions.

drawdown.definition: A fall from a previous high, in percent. After a −50% drawdown the price must rise +100% to get back.

leverage.definition: Investing with borrowed money. It multiplies gains and losses on your own money, and the loan stays even when the investment falls.

risk-capacity.definition: How much money you could lose without it hurting your daily life or your plans.

leading-room.definition: A Korean name for paid chat rooms that sell “sure” stock tips. Regulators warn about them because many are used to hype stocks.

pump-and-dump.definition: Someone buys a stock cheaply, hypes it so others buy and the price rises, then sells. When the buying stops, the price crashes.

diversification.definition: Spreading money over many different investments, so that one failure is only a small part of what you own.

concentration-risk.definition: The risk of having a large share of your money in one place: one company, one sector or one bet.
